newsitem.title: FINLAND: US expects NATO-Russia charter by July--US diplomat.
newsitem.headline: US expects NATO-Russia charter by July--US diplomat.

text.p: The U.S. expects final agreement on the NATO-Russia charter outlined by Presidents Boris Yeltsin and Bill Clinton last week to be reached before NATO's Madrid summit in July, a U.S. diplomat said on Monday.

"The discussion about NATO-Russia language for the charter will be something that Secretary General (Javier) Solana in Brussels will be working with and we are hoping that will come to fruition before the July NATO summit," U.S. Ambassador to Helsinki Derek Shearer told a briefing.

At their summit in Helsinki last Friday, the two presidents agreed to disagree on NATO's expansion plans but vowed to press ahead with the charter to set a new relationship between Russia and the pact.
Clinton was due to travel to Europe in May and would if necessary make a special trip to the continent so that a final deal could be signed before summer, Shearer said.
He echoed the U.S. administration's earlier comments that the summit held last Friday was a success overall, and said it was important that the issue of NATO enlargement had been "depoliticised".
The presidents had not made any deal on which countries could apply to join NATO, he said. "There was absolutely no agreement about which country could or couldn't (apply)," Shearer said.
